searchText: Yes, devnet-2 👍🏻 I forgot to share this earlier 😛 Here is how you can do sync tests moving forward: https://github.com/ethpandaops/kurtosis-sync-test?tab=readme-ov-file#peerdas-sync-test it prints out a nice summary for you CL clients, please review this PR for fusaka-devnet-2: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4354 Question: If we are still in Electra, and we encounter an ENR with `nfd`, do we drop the peer, or we ignore that field and validate the rest? I don't think it should exist pre-Fulu, but if this does happen I think ignoring the field might be best. cc <@795439202732867594> Lgtm. Prysm already implemented here: https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/15365 lmk if there's another implemention somewhere so I can try kurtosis something is up with the reth hosts <@412614104222531604> ui glitch? there was a misconfugiration in CLI params that caused failure on startup thanks for the info! <@412614104222531604> `column-syncer-767aca4`, our devnet 1 image btw here in spec shouldn't we change the spec following deprecation of `compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs`? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/fulu/validator.md#get_data_column_sidecars I'm planning to kill `fusaka-devnet-0` by end of today. Please yell if you are opposing this. <@412614104222531604> please enable debug logs in nimbusEL rolling https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4371 Also, some blob schedule requirements <@680234424037670912> suggested: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4370 Please review if/when you have time. Sorry i was wrong, it's not reconstruction, it's proposal, right? so getPayloadV5 is used, not getBlobsV2 which is used for reconstruction only Oops okay. Will update this later. We should probably discuss the timing of when it should be set… we want to make sure fulu is all good straight away on fork I had the same question. I believe as long as blob schedule does not backport to support deneb and electra then we should be safe. Otherwise we will be looking at potential network split
